newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast spot prods soften with NYMEX Friday.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast spot prods soften with NYMEX Friday.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot product prices softened Friday under pressure from lower energy futures with volume light as traders returned from an industry function in Houston, Texas, brokers said.
"We've got a combination of golf, people coming and going from Houston. People have written this week off," one brokers said.
The futures market, which influences spot trade, dampened values with unleaded gasoline for June delivery falling 2.11 cents a gallon Friday to 60.52 cents.
CARB unleaded gasoline fell one cent to 66/67 cents, under pressure from gasoline futures and a 31 cent a gallon fall in crude oil for June delivery.
Traders said gasoline would stay under pressure given last week's 1.4-million-barrel build in West Coast gasoline stocks, which put supplies at 28.1 million barrels last week.
After stagnating early Thursday, CARB diesel in Los Angeles fell about two cents a gallon 60.50/62 cents a gallon, adding to last week's 10 percent decline in prices.

Supplies were ample. Distillate stocks, including diesel, stood at 11.5 million barrels, nearly the same as last week's levels which saw a year-on-year increase of 1.1 million barrels, according to the American Petroleum Institute (API).
